quotes.text: So here's the simplest definition. Windows 365 is a full Windows desktop that runs in Microsoft's cloud, not on your device.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a crisp one-sentence definition of what Windows 365 is.

quotes.text: With Windows 365, your data never leaves the cloud PC. It stays in Microsoft's data center behind enterprise grade security. The personal device becomes what's called a dumb terminal.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the core security argument for Cloud PCs on personal devices.

quotes.text: Conditional access policies take this even further. You can set up rules that block access to company resources unless the user is connected through their cloud PC.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows a concrete control pattern that makes the Cloud PC the single point of access.

quotes.text: If you want simplicity and you have full time users, go with Windows 365. If you have large deployments with variable usage patterns like shift workers, part time staff or seasonal peaks, AVD can be cheaper
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a simple decision rule between Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop.

quotes.text: If you manage contractors, remote workers or a BYOD environment, Windows 365 gives you the control of corporate hardware without the cost and complexity.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the key takeaway and target audience of the episode.

chapters.title: A computer you access from any screen
What Windows 365 is and how it works

takeaways: Windows 365 streams a full Windows desktop from Microsoft's cloud, so the device in your hands is only a window into your Cloud PC.

Because data stays in the Cloud PC, redirections are off by default and Conditional Access can enforce access only through the Cloud PC, contractors and BYOD users can work without company data landing on personal devices.

Windows 365 offers predictable per-user pricing that pays off most for contractors, seasonal staff and mixed workforces, while Azure Virtual Desktop can be cheaper for large, variable deployments but is more complex to run.
hook: Buying, imaging and shipping laptops for contractors, remote workers and seasonal staff is slow, costly and risky for your data. This episode explains Windows 365 in plain English for business owners and IT decision makers: what a Cloud PC is, how Business and Enterprise differ, what it costs and how it compares to laptops and Azure Virtual Desktop.
